decomp.anything

Reverse engineering

Pick your binary.
Your agents take it apart.

Games, Windows and Linux programs, apps, firmware — anything you own. Matchable targets rebuild byte for byte; anything else becomes a project where agents read its functions and record findings. Every match is checked against your copy.

  1. Drop your binarydecomp.anything finds every function, or opens it with REA
  2. Free matches firstthe autopilot tries a machine draft of each game function
  3. Agents do the restClaude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode or any API model

Drop your binary

ROM, disc image, .exe/.dll, ELF or any binary · PDB/MAP/symbols/trace only if the game shipped them · or choose files

GameCubeWiiN64PS1PS2GBADSPCLinux

★ recommended: the most tested path to a full decomp you can port and mod · a lit chip means its tools are installed

Starting context optional: companions beside the binary are added automatically

Paths are on this computer. A path import also finds a PDB/MAP beside the program automatically. Everything can still be added later in Settings.

Public decomps

    
Continue a public decomp

    
Paste a community decomp's repository and add your own copy of its game. Before anything is cloned, decomp.anything shows what the project says about AI and contributions: every project decides that for itself. Your fork stays on this computer; decomp.anything never pushes it or opens pull requests.

    

    
decomp.dev, the community's home for matching decompilation progress, made by encounter (who also makes decomp-toolkit and objdiff, two of the tools decomp.anything is built on), retired its project directory on 15 October 2026. Each project's page there still has its history, files and contributors.

Contents

      

        
Every file in the archive. Analyze a binary or nested archive as its own target; text and assets stay readable here.

        

        

      

    


    

      
Features

        

      

        
A feature is a route, string, IPC channel or module traced through a JavaScript or Electron app. Every part the trace reaches becomes a work item; its findings roll into the summary.

        

        

      

    


    

      
Sources

        

      

        
The code this project has recovered: files from source maps, archives, or functions matched byte for byte, and the code agents reconstruct where none of that exists. Verified code is proved against the original; reconstructed code is kept apart, never counted as a match.

            Compiler
            
        
            
          
            Every function is built with this compiler and these flags. If almost nothing matches, the game was probably built with another compiler or flags.
            
          
          
          
            
          
            
          
            
        
            
      
            
      
            
        
            Project facts
            
        
            
          
            Re-read the target and refresh the facts agents work from: the detected build, version, language and inferred flags, the library/CRT classification, and INTAKE.md. Verified matches and function boundaries are never changed.
            
          
            
          
            
        
            
      
            
      
            
        
            Function boundaries
            
        
            
          
            32-bit programs have no function table. An older import could cut a function into fragments at its own branch targets; merge those pieces back into the function they belong to. Matched functions are never changed.
            
          
            
          
            
        
            
      
            
      
            
        
            Symbols & types
            
        
            
          
            Import names and types that already exist beside the target: a PDB, ELF DWARF, a MAP file or symbol_addrs.txt. Debug names replace automatic sub_/func_ names; types go into the shared header.
            
          
          
            
          
            
          
            
        
            
      
            
      
            
        
            Runtime coverage
            
        
            
          
            Import a debugger, emulator or profiler trace: one address per line, a CSV with address/count, or JSON. Counts are added to the functions that contain those addresses; use the Coverage filter or list_hot to prioritize.
            
          
          
            
          
            
          
            
        
            
      
            
      
            
        
            Compare versions
            
        
            
          
            Point at another copy of this program (a patch, demo or port). Functions are matched by normalized instructions, so moved addresses don't break the comparison.
